text: Same ambulance. America: twelve seventy-seven. Japan: zero. Why?
Twelve seventy-seven is the average U.S. charge for an emergency ambulance ride. Before mileage.
And ground ambulances aren't covered by the No Surprises Act.
So if it's out of network, the bill can still surprise you.
In Japan, you call one-one-nine, and the ride is free. Local taxes pay for it.
So why is America so expensive?
Reason one: prices vary by state. California: fourteen sixty-one on average.
Reason two: insurers allow about seven fifty-eight. Out of network, you can be billed the rest.
Japan has a catch too. Some cities charge seventy-seven hundred yen, about fifty dollars, if you're not admitted.
Why? Too many calls for small stuff. In Matsusaka, calls dropped ten percent.
Back home, one study found ambulance use fell seven percent after Uber came to town.
Twelve seventy-seven versus zero. Or fifty bucks, worst case.
Would you call nine-one-one… or an Uber? Comment below.
